Reword to say the shop markets gluten-free as a lifestyle attribute, which is weaker evidence of allergen awareness than the record implies. why: The record treats the GF story as one marketing blog post, but the shop's operator-maintained Gurunavi menu labels roughly fifteen dishes 【グルテンフリー】 in a deliberate two-tier scheme that also marks 【グルテンフリー・ベジタリアン】 — 鶏肉チマキ, よだれ鶏, 蒸し鶏のネギソース, クラゲきゅうり, 麻辣ピーナッツ, 青菜の塩ナムル, 自家製極太メンマ, 胡麻ダレ冷やしトマト, パクチーだけのサラダ and more, most of them cold or steamed and never near the fryer. That is precisely the protocol definition of options: named adaptable dishes with no special handling. It cannot go above options — every source is the operator's own voice, which the HARD RULE caps — and the options text must carry two warnings the evidence now supports outright: the kitchen is a wheat water-dumpling line, and the shop deep-fries wheat gyoza and wheat spring rolls in the same oil as its own GF-labelled 油淋鶏, so that one labelled dish should be avoided. Left at ask, a celiac in Shinjuku is told nothing about fifteen dishes the operator has already labelled for them.
